quantity: Weighted finite-population standard deviation of each group contribution to predicted log odds, calculated separately for each joint posterior draw.
point_estimate: Posterior median of the standard deviation. The SD at the posterior mode is also exported separately; it is not used as the median.
interval: Approximate 95% marginal posterior interval from 512 saved joint Laplace draws.
reference: Equal benchmark strata, equal models within benchmark, equal tasks within benchmark/model, equal observed harnesses within benchmark/model/task; repeated attempts do not increase reference weight.
intercept: Zero spread by definition because the intercept is constant across all reference rows. Its baseline log odds are not plotted.
limitations: This measures effect magnitude, not average direction. A group can have zero signed mean and large spread.
Spread is nonnegative. Positive credible bounds alone are not a valid test against a zero-variance null.
This finite-population spread is derived from the existing coefficients; it is not a newly learned random-effect variance hyperparameter.
Groups can be correlated and their variances do not add to a unique explained-variance decomposition.
Allocation between main and interaction effects depends on the existing parameterization and fixed priors; this chart does not establish causal or out-of-sample importance.
